rows.title: Lack of Visibility & Communication Between Mobility and Sales.There is a critical lack of visibility for the Mobility team regarding ongoing activities within Salesforce (SF), which Sales exclusively
rows.issue: Lack of Visibility & Communication Between Mobility and Sales.There is a critical lack of visibility for the Mobility team regarding ongoing activities within Salesforce (SF), which Sales exclusively uses. Meanwhile, Mobility operates in Zendesk (ZD), leading to a disconnect between both teams.  Key Challenges: Sales operates only in SF, while Mobility operates only in ZD, preventing seamless access to shared case details. Mobility can escalate cases to Sales in SF, but has zero visibility into the progress, updates, or resolutions. Sales does not proactively communicate updates back to Mobility, creating delays and misalignment.
rows.proposed_resolution: To bridge this gap, we can implement one of the following solutions:  SF-ZD Integration – Implement a system that syncs key case updates between Salesforce and Zendesk, ensuring both teams have real-time visibility into relevant cases. This would allow Mobility to track case progress without needing direct access to SF.  Slack-Based Communication Flow – If integrating SF and ZD is not feasible in the short term, we can set up a dedicated Slack channel where each case triggers a thread, automatically tagging the relevant Sales and Mobility POCs. This would allow real-time communication, reducing delays and misalignment.  Either of these approaches would enhance transparency, streamline case management, and improve collaboration between teams

rows.title: Sweden Work permit requirements: We are often missing the mandatory insurances (health+pension) required for employees to work in Sweden when apply for an employer sponsored permit. Mobility/HRX need
rows.issue: Sweden Work permit requirements: We are often missing the mandatory insurances (health+pension) required for employees to work in Sweden when apply for an employer sponsored permit. Mobility/HRX need to flag these to CSM to get approved by the client to be added to the contract, and then HRX needs to add it manually before e.g. an off-platform EA can be used for the work permit application. Another, related issue to Sweden work permits is that our vendor typically recommends the removal of probation period as otherwise the work permit will be only granted for the probation period duration, and then an extension is needed. Similarly, we always need the client to approve this if they have added it to the contract upon creating it. They must also be informed about the double-deposit applied in this case, which CSMs again might not be aware of.  Clients are obviously not too keen to learn all about these details after the process is already ongoing.
rows.proposed_resolution: Ideally, when clients are creating a contract for an EOR to Sweden who required a work permit, an automated information about the mandatory insurances as well as information on the recommendation of probation period removal would be great. rows.title: Letters from Deel Portugal to speed up the renewal process
rows.issue: Letters from Deel Portugal to speed up the renewal process
rows.proposed_resolution: Currently, in Portugal, many employees request a letter signed by Deel to expedite their appointment dates for the temporary renewal process. These letters typically need to mention the necessity of renewing their permit for compliance reasons and to facilitate travel abroad.  Current Situation: 1. Due to delays in renewal appointments, employees cannot travel outside Portugal once their residence permit has expired. Many need to travel for work purposes. The customized options on the platform, such as a No-Objection Letter (NOC) or a Business Letter, do not apply here. Employees often request a personal letter with a template in Portuguese. This requirement causes escalations, multiple exchanges in support tickets, and frustration, as they feel it should be straightforward. 2. Another point of frustration (related to point 1) is the platform's requirement to request the new document 180 days before the expiry date. Currently, most employees cannot begin the renewal process earlier than 90 days before expiration, often only once their temporary residence has expired.  Actions Taken: 1. A basic template has been sent for legal review as the initial step. 2. A request has been made to the Product team to trigger the renewal process at least 90 days before the expiration date.  Next Steps: 1. Customize a generic note (with basic information) that employees can download and present when scheduling their appointments. 2. Ensure that right-to-work cases can be initiated at least 90 days before expiration.

rows.title: The new resignation flow is confusing and lacks clarity, resulting in multiple escalations. For example, in a recent case, the employee had not yet signed the resignation letter, so HRX did not comple
rows.issue: The new resignation flow is confusing and lacks clarity, resulting in multiple escalations. For example, in a recent case, the employee had not yet signed the resignation letter, so HRX did not complete the process. However, HRX confirmed that we could proceed with the end date, assuming the employee would sign the letter with that date. Instead, this action triggered a notification to the client indicating that the resignation had been finalized.  As a result, the client believed the employee’s termination was official as of June 2, while on our end, the process was still incomplete due to the missing employee signature. This created a clear misalignment: the client saw fromhis side: end date June 2nd, whereas on the our side, the employee was showing in progress, with an end date that wasn't finalised. .
rows.proposed_resolution: The resignation flow should follow a straightforward structure, as it did in the past—where each step was completed one at a time before proceeding to the next. Currently, all actions are displayed on a single page, which makes the process unclear and difficult to navigate. It’s very unintuitive to understand what needs to be checked, where to check it, or what actions are required. This layout increases the likelihood of human error.  Additionally, when attempting to cancel a resignation, the only available option is “Cancel with the same values,” which is misleading. For example, if we only want to change the end date, we still have to select “Cancel with the same values”—even though the end date is being updated, meaning the values are not the same. Only after selecting this option can the user proceed to make the necessary change.  These issues could be avoided with a more guided, step-by-step flow and clear, accurate options—such as “Cancel and restart with different values” or “Cancel and keep the same values.”

rows.title: Hiring EU/EEU/Swiss nationals in Romania: repetitive problem blocking the onboarding.  The RTW checks for EU/EEU/Swiss nationals look quite simple: the candidate is an EU/EEU/Swiss national, and it me
rows.issue: Hiring EU/EEU/Swiss nationals in Romania: repetitive problem blocking the onboarding.  The RTW checks for EU/EEU/Swiss nationals look quite simple: the candidate is an EU/EEU/Swiss national, and it means the candidate has free access to the labor market and can be onboarded after completing the onboarding checklist and providing required information.   During the onboarding the Platform asks the EE to provide a “personal identification number”, called in Romanian an CNP (Codul Numeric Personal), which is a tax code required for non-Romanian for their day-to-day life in Romania, and we need that CNP of a candidate to be able to register an EA with such EE.   If the EE has never had a Residence permit in Romania, then he does not have a CNP in Romania.  To be able to obtain a CNP, the EE who is an EU/EEU/Swiss needs to obtain the Registration Certificate (Immigration requirement for EU nationals staying more than 90 days in Romania).  To be able to obtain the Registration Certificate it is required to provide the Romanian authorities with:   a) The EA (original and copy) or an attestation issued by the employer (original) - cannot be provided by Deel until the EE completes the onboarding process and provides the CNP;   b) A screenshot from the General Register of Employees showing the section related to the employment contract, stamped and signed by the employer to confirm the authenticity of the document. - the registration of the EA within the authorities, which cannot be arranged without the EE having a CNP.   The EE needs the EA and registration of the EA to be able to obtain the CNP,  and for Deel to onboard the EE, provide the EA, and register the EA, the EE should provide the CNP for Deel.  We need a solution here because the EEs are stuck. Maybe there is a way how to obtain the CNP without the documents mentioned above, but we are not aware of the process and we cannot guide the EEs.
rows.proposed_resolution: Either we don’t onboard the EEs without the CNP (then who is going to check it? Should it be a part of the RTW process?), or we should understand if there is any way to obtain the CNP without the documents mentioned above, and provide the EEs with clear guidance.

rows.issue: Problem We’ve had several recent cases where the Job Description (JD) included onsite activities or did not align with the Job Title (JT). At the quote stage, the JT is usually flagged and corrected if it doesn’t meet criteria, but the JD remains unchanged. Automatically flag and create a task for the Legal team before EA is generated.  Proactive Approach  Add a pre-onboarding compliance review step to catch inconsistencies between JT and JD earlier.  Ensure both JT and JD are aligned and compliant before contracts move forward.  Visibility for Teams  Improve visibility into EA generation even when no redlines are present, so potential issues can be caught sooner.

rows.title: In certain countries, local labor laws prohibit employers to review or modify their existing benefit plans if that action could lead to a reduction or removal of benefits. Under these regulations, any
rows.issue: In certain countries, local labor laws prohibit employers to review or modify their existing benefit plans if that action could lead to a reduction or removal of benefits. Under these regulations, any downgrade or elimination of a benefit plan - such as health insurance or other employment-related coverages - constitutes a substantial modification of employment conditions. This makes it unlawful to prompt clients or employees to “reconfirm” their selections in a way that implies potential loss of benefits or sending mass comms with the option to downgrade. Our current process, which prompts clients to validate or change their benefit selections, unintentionally conflicts with these legal restrictions, creating compliance risk and triggering escalations from local teams and clients.
rows.proposed_resolution: Ideal Solution to Prevent This Type of Escalation: The process should be aligned with local labor regulations by removing or adapting prompts that ask Clients to review or confirm their benefits in countries where such actions are restricted. Communications should clearly state that existing benefits will continue automatically unless a legally justified and documented change is initiated by the employer and accepted by the employee.     A compliance review must be embedded in all global benefit workflows to identify and flag country-specific limitations before launch. Additionally, country-specific guidance and training should be provided to internal teams and clients to ensure consistent compliance and avoid future escalations.     Any mass communications related to benefit renewals in these countries should only promote the option to upgrade coverage—never to downgrade or request reconfirmation. Any change involving a reduction or removal of coverage, including dependent coverage, must be supported by documented consent from the employee. Processes should therefore enable formal amendments in cases where the client explicitly requests a downgrade or removal.     To strengthen compliance, a dedicated project should be launched with the legal teams in each country to systematically identify where it is illegal to downgrade or not renew benefits. This will create a definitive, country-specific reference to guide communications and system workflows, ensuring adherence to local laws.

rows.issue: We’ve identified an ongoing issue with clients who have their own Time Off app integrated with our platform. Since these are external applications, we’re unable to apply or enforce the same configuration and workflow rules that we have within our own system. As a result, we lose visibility over mandatory documentation, such as sick leave reports, when an employee is on sick leave. This creates operational challenges, as we have to manually request the documents in each case, or risk missing important compliance information due to oversight. We should consider how to improve the information flow or set clearer expectations with clients to ensure all required documents are properly submitted and tracked, even when using external systems.
rows.proposed_resolution: To address this, we can proactively notify active clients who are using external Time Off apps about the issue and the importance of sharing mandatory documentation (such as sick leave reports) directly with us. Alternatively, we can suggest that clients adjust the configuration of their Time Off app so that these types of absences automatically trigger a document upload or notification to our team. This way, we can ensure we receive all required documentation, maintain compliance, and avoid manual follow-ups or missing information in the future. We already have a report listing all clients who have an external Time Off app integrated with us, which can help us monitor and prioritize communication with them.  For new clients, they need to be informed either by CSM, Product of the engineering team handling before the integration is enabled, that for X countries the document needs to be enabled as mandatory from their side. Please run a project for all countries and types of leaves that need required documents to have a country-specific reference guide.

rows.title: The current platform setup for Greece supports only “Full Time,” “Part Time,” and “Rotational” classifications. “Intermittent” employment — legally distinct in Greece — is missing entirely. As a resul
rows.issue: The current platform setup for Greece supports only “Full Time,” “Part Time,” and “Rotational” classifications. “Intermittent” employment — legally distinct in Greece — is missing entirely. As a result, contracts that are legally intermittent or rotational are being incorrectly recorded as “part time,” both during hiring and in contract submission.  This misclassification creates multiple issues: • Payroll cannot communicate accurate working hours for rotational or intermittent roles while the system forces them into “part time.” • PTO is calculated incorrectly because intermittent and rotational roles have different statutory accrual rules, which are not reflected in the platform. • Greek labor law requires rotational employees to receive additional pay (e.g., 1 extra day per 3 days of 8-hour work), but the platform cannot detect or apply this. • The quoting flow cannot identify these employment types, leading to incorrect contract context, misaligned PTO, and compliance risks.  These issues stem from incorrect or incomplete employment type configuration for Greece, causing repeated manual fixes and legal exposure.
rows.proposed_resolution: Introduce proper employment classifications for Greece: Full Time, Part Time, Intermittent, Rotational, reflecting national labor law.  Enable the quoting flow to automatically detect working-hour patterns and assign the correct contract category (as already implemented in markets like Italy).  Ensure the contract template displays the correct employment type and corresponding PTO rules.  Update PTO calculation logic so intermittent and rotational workers receive the correct statutory accruals.  Impact: Accurate legal classification, correct PTO calculations, elimination of recurring manual fixes, reduced payroll discrepancies, and protection from compliance risk. PF was raised in august https://letsdeel.atlassian.net/browse/PF-15546

rows.title: In Spain, the Social Security Number (SSN) is mandatory to start employment. Employees must have it before the contract starts, as social security registration needs to be done in advance. We cannot c
rows.issue: In Spain, the Social Security Number (SSN) is mandatory to start employment. Employees must have it before the contract starts, as social security registration needs to be done in advance. We cannot countersign contracts without this required data point. Some employees do not yet have a Spanish SSN: EU citizens moving to Spain for the first time, or visa-sponsored employees relocated to Spain. The SSN can be obtained in two ways: the employee requests it themselves, or the company requests it before the start date. Requesting it independently has been difficult for employees due to Spanish bureaucracy, though some succeed. If employees face blockers or are rejected, they reach out to Deel for assistance. If the company requests the SSN, the effective start date of the new SSN must be within the next five days, otherwise the SSN expires and a new request is required. We also require a mandatory compliance document showing the SSN, which must match the number entered in Payroll and compliance details. This ensures employees upload a valid number, not a dummy. The current regex validation is: ^(?<na>0[1-9]|[1-4][0-9]|5[0-2])(?<nb>\d{8})(?<nc>\d{2})$ and in order to remove the compliance document, we need our validation tool to actually makes calculations following a calculation code like the one here: Social Security Validation Code: https://intervia.com/doc/validar-numeros-de-la-seguridad-social/ Errors in entering SSNs can cause delays, and Spain does not allow backdating. Currently, the process requires manual intervention: HRX collects forms (TA1, passport/NIE, work permit), submits to Payroll, and ensures proper entry. Once processed, the employee enters the SSN in Payroll and compliance details, uploads a document showing the number, and onboarding is completed.
rows.proposed_resolution: Provide a flag during onboarding to indicate the employee does not have a Spanish SSN.   Trigger an alert to HRX/Payroll when this occurs.   Allow employees to upload the completed TA1 form and documents directly within the workflow, so it flows automatically to the responsible team.   Incorporate the 5-day rule, ensuring the SSN’s effective start date is within 5 days of the contract start. If the employee starts in 2 months, the contract cannot be countersigned until the week before the start date.   Impact:  Automating and productizinf the SSN request in Deel Spain will create a smoother onboarding experience, reduce manual work for HRX and Payroll, and ensure compliance by guaranteeing all Spanish employees have a valid SSN before their start date.

rows.issue: In several countries, there are more public holidays listed than the number employees are legally entitled to take (e.g. 22 available holidays, but only 13 can be taken). At the moment, the Time Off product only supports a static list of mandatory holidays, without the ability to cap how many holidays an employee can actually select.
rows.proposed_resolution: Because of this limitation:  Employees cannot directly select eligible holidays from the Time Off page.  Workarounds (e.g. removing holidays from the People section and creating “Regional Holiday” leave types, as done in Nepal) force employees and clients to:  Check FAQs to know eligibility  Manually apply for leave  Manually approve requests  This leads to confusion, poor user experience, repeated escalations, and increased dependency on Legal and HRX, even when the legal logic is already clear.  Impact:  Repeated tickets and escalations for something that should be system-controlled  Inconsistent employee experience across countries  Higher operational overhead for HRX, Legal, and clients  Employees are blocked or unsure how to correctly apply for legally allowed holidays  Proposed Solution (Product Feedback): Enhance the Public Holidays section in Time Off with the following functionality:  Keep the full backend list of mandatory/public holidays (e.g. 22 holidays).  Allow employees to select holidays from a dropdown list when applying for time off.  Introduce a hard system cap so employees can only select up to the legally authorized number (e.g. 13 holidays).  Ensure this selection happens directly on the Time Off page, without relying on FAQs or manual workarounds.  This removes ambiguity, prevents incorrect submissions, and eliminates unnecessary approvals and escalations.  Outcome:  Legally compliant by design  Significantly improved employee and client experience  Reduced escalations to Legal and HRX  Scalable solution across multiple countries with similar rules

rows.title: Cal.com | Employee Experience Aspect
rows.issue: Cal.com | Employee Experience Aspect
rows.proposed_resolution: In the current Cal.com call booking flow, employees are asked to select the type of query and indicate whether they have an existing HRX thread.  When an employee selects “No existing HRX ticket,” the context they provide during booking is not surfaced to HRX in a visible or actionable way. As a result, once the call is created, HRX often needs to follow up via email to ask the employee to restate the same query they already submitted.  This creates an unnecessary loop:  The employee explains their issue during the booking process  That context is not available to HRX upfront  The employee is asked again to provide the same information  Resolution is delayed and requires additional back-and-forth  From an employee experience perspective, this repetition can be frustrating. Employees feel they have already done the work to clearly explain their concern, only to be asked to repeat it, which can reduce trust in the process and make the interaction feel inefficient and transactional rather than supportive.  From an HRX execution standpoint, the lack of upfront visibility also slows down resolution. If the employee’s original input were automatically captured as an internal note on the Cal.com booking (when no HRX ticket exists), HRX could immediately:  Route payroll-related topics to Payroll  Address HRX queries proactively  Reduce follow-up emails and handling time  Overall, this small gap in the booking flow has a disproportionate impact on both employee satisfaction and first-touch resolution efficiency. rows.issue: Creation of unified slack tag/ handle per country with multiple COs. Without a unified Slack handle per country, teams in channels like Revolut, Managed HR, and Hypercare risk pinging a single CO who may be OOO while other available COs for that same country are missed.
rows.proposed_resolution: Create a dedicated Slack group handle for each country that has multiple Country Owners (e.g., @hrx-netherlands, @hrx-spain, @hrx-uk, @hrx-us, etc.), add those handles to Column G of the HRX Onboarding Control Sheet, and enforce the use of the group handle — rather than individual @ mentions — in all internal onboarding channels.
